name: ReachStream
summary: B2B contact database with a published price instead of a quote: unlimited contact and company views on every tier, with the meter running on exports rather than on looking. Annual billing takes 20% off the price and changes nothing about the allowance. Read on their own pricing page on 10 September 2026.
best_for: small sales and marketing teams that want a B2B contact database with a published price rather than a quote, and whose volume is predictable enough to size in exports a month — the tier below the ones where ZoomInfo and Cognism start.
skip_if: you need more than three seats without an enterprise conversation; your volume is spiky, because nothing on the page tells you what an extra credit costs; or your market is outside the sectors where their data is strongest, in which case ask for a sample against your own ICP before you pay.
honest_knock: The meter is on exporting, not on looking, and that is the number to size before you pick a tier. Contact and company views are unlimited on every plan including the free one, so the demo will feel generous; what you actually pay for is pulling those records out, and separately for revealing an email address, which is a second meter the plan cards do not put next to the first. Free gives 100 exports and 200 email views a month, which is a sample rather than a workflow. The second thing to check is seats: Starter and Pro both include exactly one, so a two-person sales team is on Business at $99 a month before it needs the extra credits. Credits do not roll over: the FAQ, re-read on 19 September 2026, says unused credits reset at the start of each new billing cycle, so a plan sized for a busy month is simply wasted in a quiet one. That same question answered the other way on 10 September, which is reason enough to check it yourself before you commit. Underbuying is no clearer either: two figures on the page are not explained anywhere — Starter and Pro promise to "unlock an extra $250 / $500 worth of data", which is priced in dollars rather than in credits or records — and the cost of a credit once you run out is not published at all.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-10 in a browser on reachstream.com/prospect/pricing/ with both billing toggles, and re-verified against that same page on 19 September 2026 -- every amount, credit allowance and seat count below is unchanged; only the credit-rollover answer in the FAQ has flipped) Five tiers in USD. Free is $0 with 100 export credits and 200 email views a month (1,200 and 2,400 a year). Starter is $39 a month, or $29 on annual billing, for 5,000 export credits a month (60,000 a year). Pro is $59 or $49 for 10,000 a month. Business is $99 or $79 for 20,000 a month (240,000 a year) and, for the first time, up to three seats instead of one. Enterprise is quote-only. The annual discount is a flat 20% on the price and nothing else: the credit allowance is identical either way. Two meters run separately — export credits are spent downloading to CSV or syncing to a CRM, email credits are spent revealing an address in the platform or the Chrome extension — while contact and company insight views are unlimited on every tier including Free. Email views are unlimited on all paid tiers. The FAQ, re-read on 19 September 2026, states that unused credits do not roll over and that they reset at the start of each new billing cycle -- on 10 September that same question answered the other way round, so size the plan for an ordinary month rather than a busy one and confirm the rule before you buy. It also states that direct-dial and mobile numbers are included on Starter, Pro and Business. Note that the main /pricing/ page carries no figures at all — it only routes you to Prospect or Email Verifier — and that the site answers a plain HTTP request with 403, so the figures above come from a browser reading of the Prospect pricing page one level down.

compare_with.name: RocketReach
compare_with.why: RocketReach sells the same shape of thing — a contact database with self-serve tiers — and both publish their prices, which already puts them in a different bracket from the quote-only end of this market. The difference is what the meter counts. ReachStream meters exports and leaves views unlimited, so the question is how many records you pull; RocketReach meters lookups, so the question is how often you search. If your team browses widely and exports rarely, ReachStream is the cheaper shape. If you export in bulk from a narrow list, check the per-record maths on both before assuming the lower headline price wins
